teaser.text: Fastenal supplies the industrial parts, equipment, and replenishment systems that help factories, construction crews, and maintenance teams keep working. Its business begins with the humble bolt but ends with a managed purchasing relationship that can reach across a customer’s sites.

blocks.heading: Where could Fastenal’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $50.61 in October 2027. Including dividends, that is a -1% return. The weighted price is $52.40 in October 2028. The return is then +5%. The weighted price reaches $53.70 in October 2029, for a +10% return.
At October 2029, the bear outcome is $34.05. The bull outcome is $75.22. Today’s reference price is $52.00. The bear probability is 25%. The base probability is 55%. The bull probability is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Fastenal?

paragraphs.text: Base earnings rise from $1,616 million to $1,765 million. They reach $1,905 million in the third year. This reflects contract-customer growth, larger-site productivity and operating leverage, while margins remain near recent normalized levels. The bear path is $1,411 million initially and $1,414 million thereafter. It reaches $1,450 million as manufacturing demand, customer mix and price-cost pressure weaken margins. The bull path starts at $1,652 million and reaches $1,889 million. It ends at $2,150 million only if installations, capacity and collections all improve.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Fastenal really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending was $245.3 million, leaving free cash flow of $1,050.6 million. Stock compensation absorbed another $8.4 million. On that basis, “real free cash flow” was $1,042.2 million because shares paid to employees still dilute shareholders.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Fastenal today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio divides the share price by earnings per share. Fastenal trades at 41.9 times its last twelve months’ earnings and 37.0 times expected earnings over the next twelve months. That gap implies roughly 13% earnings growth. Q3 sales grew 15.5%, while pricing contributed about 2.4 percentage points, so growth beyond pricing did much of the work.

blocks.heading: Is Fastenal's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash left after operating needs and investment. Fastenal’s free-cash-flow yield is 1.8%, while its dividend yield is 2.0%. Accounting profit can arrive first: Fastenal might deliver $100 of bolts today, record the sale, and collect the money next month. During rapid growth, unpaid invoices and inventory absorb cash; receivables rose 19.9% year over year. Q3 operating cash flow was $421.6 million, while disclosed free cash flow was $349.6 million against $298.2 million of dividends. The dividend was covered in that quarter, but future growth remains the larger part of the investment case.

paragraphs.text: October sales, due November 5, 2026, will show whether September’s slower daily-sales growth was temporary or a demand warning. Year-end 2026 results will test whether signings, Digital Footprint, and the investment program meet guidance, and whether installed systems produce profitable demand. Collections and inventory will determine how quickly growth funds investment and shareholder payments; the next scheduled note repayment is $50.0 million on May 15, 2027.

blocks.heading: What has Fastenal guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management targets $310–330 million of net investment in property and equipment for 2026. It also targets 27,000–29,000 weighted FASTBin and FASTVend signings, programs that place supply bins or vending machines at customer sites. The targets include a 62–63% Digital Footprint—the share of sales made through digital tools and systems—and a 24.6% ongoing tax rate.

paragraphs.text: Fastenal has reported progress in large-account selling and higher profit, alongside weaker conversion of earnings into free cash flow. The promise is therefore mixed, not broken: owners are best served when profitable growth arrives with a satisfactory return on the money committed to achieving it.

blocks.heading: What do Fastenal's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Operating income and EPS rose year over year in each of the first three quarters of 2026. The turn is therefore in growth and operating efficiency, while pricing recovery and collection efficiency remain incomplete.

blocks.heading: What should Fastenal watchers watch next?

paragraphs.text: The December year end will test whether device signings, digital transactions and delayed investment reached their targets. These measures need to be read together. Lower spending could mean projects slipped again, while more digital activity could simply mean existing orders changed channels. The important question is whether installed systems bring additional purchasing through a more productive network.
